newsitem.title: JAPAN: Pace of decline in Japan trade surplus slowing-MOF.
newsitem.headline: Pace of decline in Japan trade surplus slowing-MOF.

text.p: The pace of the decline in Japan's trade surplus is slowing down, the Ministry of Finance (MOF) said on Monday.
"We think that that the tempo of the decline in the trade surplus is slowing down," a MOF official said.
He added that it was difficult to forecast trade data in the coming months as the data depends on trade movements, currencies, oil prices and economic conditions at home and abroad.
However, he also explained that growth in exports has been posting two-digit increases although growth in imports continues to surpass that of exports in value terms.
The official also said strong growth in car exports was mainly due to a rebound from the low levels of the previous year, adding that the rebound may continue for some time.
He attributed the growth in car exports to brisk demand in the United States.
Strong growth in exports of semiconductor parts to the United States was seen due to strong demand there for a new type of micro-processing unit (MPU).
In calculating the figures, the ministry used a currency rate of 121.18 yen to the dollar for February 1997, against 106.38 a year earlier.
The MOF announced on Monday morning that Japan's customs-cleared trade surplus rose 6.5 percent in February from a year earlier to 686.72 billion yen, the first rise in over two years.
The trade surplus with the United States, often a source of trade friction, rose 12.3 percent in February from a year earlier to 407.35 billion yen.
The MOF official said it was the first time since November 1994 that Japan's surpluses with the United States, the European Union and Asia had risen at the same time.
